The Filipinos Do Not Yield (FDNY) Movement, along with various groups, hold a lightning protest in front of the Chinese Embassy along Sen. Gil Puyat Avenue in Makati City on Monday, May 11.

The protesters condemned the continued harassment, intimidation, and aggressive presence of Chinese ships in the West Philippine Sea, as well as China’s statement that the Philippines is “playing with fire” because of its alliances and preparations for self-defense. Protesters also held placards and burned a cardboard replica of a Chinese Coast Guard ship to express their anger. 

📸: Mark Balmores/MB

An "Impeach Sara" protest breaks out in front of the House of Representatives in Quezon City ahead of the scheduled plenary vote on Monday, May 11, 2026. 

Under the Constitution, at least 106 votes, representing one-third of the chamber, are required to officially elevate the case to the Senate, which will convene as an impeachment court for a formal trial. | via Jonathan Cellona, ABS-CBN
